data.name: Hadir
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Hadir means present or existence. It is derived from the word 'hadara' which means to be present or to exist. The name Hadir is associated with the concept of being present in the moment and acknowledging the beauty and blessings of the present.

in_arabic.name: هادِر
in_arabic.meaning: هادِر يعني حاضر و آماده، کسی که همیشه آماده است
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم هادِر من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني من يكون دائمًا حاضرًا ومتأهبًا لكل شيء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: «وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا» (الإسراء: 36)، وقد أشتق من الفعل 'هدر' الذي يعني الاستعداد والتهيؤ

in_urdu.name: ہادر
in_urdu.meaning: ہادر مطلب ہے حاضر اور مستعد، ایک ایسا شخص جو ہمیشہ تیار رہتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ہادر ایک خوبصورت نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، اس کا مطلب ہے حاضر اور آماده، یہ نام اللہ تعالیٰ کے اسماء حسنیٰ میں سے ایک ہے، اور قرآن مجید میں بھی اس کا ذکر آیا ہے، جیسے کہ سورہ اسراء میں: «وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ»

in_hindi.name: हादिर
in_hindi.meaning: हादिर का अर्थ है حاضر और तैयार, एक ऐसा व्यक्ति जो हमेशा तैयार रहता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: हादिर एक सुंदर नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, इसका अर्थ है حاضر और तैयार, यह नाम अल्लाह तआला के असमाए हुसना में से एक है, और कुरआन मजीद में भी इसका उल्लेख आया है, जैसे कि सूरह इसरा में: «وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ»

in_pashto.name: هادر
in_pashto.meaning: هادر دى چمتو او حاضر معنی دی، هغه څوک چې تل چمتو وي
in_pashto.long_meaning: هادر يو ښکلى نوم دى چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخستى شوى دى، دى نوم د الله تعالى د ښو نومونو څخه يو دى، او د قران کريم په ډېرو ځايونو کې يې ذکر شوى دى، لکه د سورة اسراء په آيت کې: «وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ»

in_english.name: Hadir
in_english.meaning: Hadir means ready and present, one who is always prepared
in_english.long_meaning: Hadir is a beautiful name derived from Arabic, it means ready and present, one who is always prepared, it is one of Allah's beautiful names, mentioned in the Quran, such as in Surah Isra: «وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ», signifying readiness and vigilance

data.cultural_impact: The name Hadir carries a rich cultural significance as it reflects the importance of living in the present in Islamic tradition. It emphasizes the value of being fully engaged in the current moment instead of dwelling on the past or worrying about the future. This mindset is encouraged in Islamic teachings as a way to find happiness and contentment in life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hadir holds great significance as it symbolizes the presence of Allah in every moment of our lives. It serves as a reminder that Allah is always with us and that we should strive to be present in His presence at all times. By being mindful of the present moment, we can strengthen our relationship with Allah and deepen our spiritual connection. Additionally, being present in the moment can lead to greater inner peace, gratitude, and joy.

historical_references.reference: The Prophet Muhammad's mosque in Medina was known as Masjid al-Haram al-Mubarak or Masjid al-Nabi (the Sacred Mosque or the Prophet's Mosque) until it was renamed to Masjid al-Hadir (the Mosque of the Lake) during the caliphate of Umar ibn Abdulaziz in the late 7th century CE. The name change was due to the construction of a large reservoir (Bir Umar) to the north of the mosque.
historical_references.context: Construction of a large reservoir north of the mosque led to its name change from Masjid al-Nabi to Masjid al-Hadir

historical_references.reference: The term 'Hadir' is also used in Islamic literature to refer to the heavenly world, the abode of Allah and his angels. It is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-An'am, 6:38, where Allah says, 'And whoever entertains the hope of meeting his Lord, he will meet him who made it (the hope), and he will be his witness: 'My servants, I have forgiven you your sins. There will be no fear upon you this day, nor will you grieve.', and they will rest in the gardens of 'Adn (Eden), and they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and they will wear green garments from the light of Allah. And the provision which they will have therein is better than that which they had.'
historical_references.context: Islamic literary reference to the concept of Hadir as the heavenly world where Allah and his angels reside
